title: A New Global Standard for Treating Heart Attacks in Women
subtitle: Medical experts have introduced a universal definition for heart attacks to ensure female patients receive faster and more accurate care.

summary.en: Global heart health organizations have agreed on a new universal definition for heart attacks. This change aims to fix long-standing problems where women received worse treatment than men. Doctors will now use lower thresholds for diagnosing heart damage in female patients. The new guidelines also recognize specific types of heart attacks that happen more often in women. This shift is expected to save lives by reducing dangerous delays in medical care.
summary.zh: 全球心臟健康組織已就心臟病發作的全新通用定義達成共識。此變革旨在解決長期以來女性接受的治療不如男性的問題。醫師未來將採用較低的門檻來診斷女性病患的心臟損傷。新指引也認可了在女性身上更常發生的特定心臟病發作類型。預計此轉變將透過減少危險的醫療延誤來挽救生命。

paragraphs.en: Medical experts have announced a major change in how doctors define and treat heart attacks. For decades, women have often received less effective care because their specific health needs were ignored or misunderstood. Now, the world’s four leading cardiovascular health groups have signed off on a new universal definition for heart attacks. This landmark agreement, announced at a major heart conference in Munich, aims to stop the deadly delays that have affected millions of women for generations.
paragraphs.zh: 醫學專家宣布了一項關於醫師如何定義與治療心臟病發作的重大變革。數十年來，女性往往因為其特殊的健康需求被忽視或誤解，而接受了效果較差的照護。如今，全球四個主要的血管健康組織已簽署了一項心臟病發作的全新通用定義。這項在慕尼黑一場大型心臟會議上宣布的里程碑式協議，旨在終止數代以來影響數百萬女性的致命延誤。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, this change is one of the biggest updates in medical procedures in many years. In the past, doctors often focused on the most common type of heart attack, which involves a blood clot blocking blood flow. However, women are much more likely to experience different types of heart attacks. These often involve a tightening of the arteries or small tears in the heart vessels. Because these types were previously seen as less important, women were often not treated as urgently as men, which sometimes made their health worse.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，這項變革是多年來醫療程序中最重大的更新之一。過去，醫師通常聚焦於最常見的心臟病發作類型，即血栓阻塞血液流動的情況。然而，女性更有可能經歷不同類型的心臟病發作，這些類型通常涉及動脈緊縮或心臟血管的小撕裂。由於這些類型先前被視為較不重要，女性往往無法像男性一樣獲得緊急治療，這有時導致她們的健康狀況惡化。

paragraphs.en: One of the most important parts of the new guidance is a change in how doctors use blood tests. When the heart is injured, it releases a protein called troponin into the blood. Until now, women were expected to reach the same high levels of this protein as men to get a diagnosis. Under the new rules, the threshold—the minimum level required for a diagnosis—will be lower for women. This will help doctors identify heart damage in female patients much faster, ensuring they get the help they need without unnecessary waiting.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新指引中最重要的部分之一，是改變了醫師使用血液檢測的方式。當心臟受損時，會釋放一種稱為肌鈣蛋白的蛋白質進入血液。在此之前，女性必須達到與男性相同的蛋白質高濃度才能獲得診斷。根據新規定，女性診斷所需的最低門檻將會降低。這將有助於醫師更快識別女性病患的心臟損傷，確保她們能獲得所需的協助，而無需進行不必要的等待。

paragraphs.en: Prof Bryan Williams, a leader at the British Heart Foundation, described the agreement as a "landmark moment." He noted that this shift will change how heart attacks are defined worldwide. By focusing on the less common causes of heart attacks that mostly affect women, doctors hope to provide better, more accurate treatment. These causes include things like emotional stress, extreme cold, or physical changes during and after pregnancy. For example, a condition called spontaneous coronary artery dissection, or SCAD, is a tear in the artery that happens in women at least 80% of the time. The new guidelines ensure that these conditions are no longer overlooked.
paragraphs.zh: 英國心臟基金會（British Heart Foundation）的領導者布萊恩·威廉斯教授（Prof Bryan Williams）將此協議描述為「里程碑時刻」。他指出，這一轉變將改變全球對心臟病發作的定義。透過聚焦於主要影響女性、但較不常見的心臟病發作原因，醫師希望能提供更好、更精確的治療。這些原因包括情緒壓力、極端寒冷，或懷孕期間及產後的生理變化。例如，一種稱為自發性冠狀動脈剝離（SCAD）的病症，即動脈撕裂，至少有百分之八十發生在女性身上。新指引確保這些病症不再被忽視。

paragraphs.en: This update builds on recent efforts to improve health outcomes for women. The Guardian Health reports that the new guidelines will upgrade three specific types of heart attacks that are up to 10 times more common in women. These include coronary artery spasm, where the artery tightens; coronary embolism, where a blockage travels to the heart; and the previously mentioned SCAD. By giving these conditions a clear, universal definition, doctors can now provide better care that targets the specific cause of the patient's problem.
paragraphs.zh: 此次更新建立在近期改善女性健康成果的努力之上。《衛報健康》報導稱，新指引將升級三種特定類型的心臟病發作，這些類型在女性身上的發生率高出十倍。其中包括冠狀動脈痙攣（動脈緊縮）、冠狀動脈栓塞（阻塞物移動至心臟），以及前述的自發性冠狀動脈剝離。透過為這些病症提供明確的通用定義，醫師現在能提供針對病患問題根源的更佳照護。

paragraphs.en: For many patients, this change will be life-changing. In the past, women were often sent home or told their symptoms were not serious enough because they did not fit the traditional "male" model of a heart attack. The new, streamlined categories will help patients understand exactly what is happening to their bodies and what steps they need to take next. This clarity is expected to reduce the fear and confusion that often follows a medical emergency.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多病患而言，這項改變將會改變她們的一生。過去，女性常因不符合傳統「男性」心臟病發作的模式，而被送回家或被告知症狀不夠嚴重。新的簡化分類將協助病患精確了解身體發生了什麼狀況，以及接下來需要採取哪些步驟。預計這種清晰度將能減少醫療緊急狀況後常伴隨的恐懼與困惑。

paragraphs.en: As the medical community begins to adopt these new standards, the focus will shift to training healthcare professionals to recognize these signs more quickly. The goal is to make sure that a woman’s heart attack is treated with the same speed and seriousness as a man’s. While it will take time for these changes to reach every hospital, experts believe this is a vital step toward equality in healthcare. By finally listening to the evidence and updating outdated rules, the medical world is taking a significant step forward in protecting the lives of women everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著醫療界開始採用這些新標準，焦點將轉向培訓醫療專業人員，以更快速地識別這些徵兆。目標是確保女性的心臟病發作能與男性獲得同等速度與嚴肅程度的治療。雖然這些變革普及到每家醫院仍需時間，但專家認為這是邁向醫療平權的關鍵一步。透過最終傾聽證據並更新過時的規則，醫學界在保護全球女性生命方面邁出了重要的一步。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To officially approve or agree to something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語在商業與正式文件中常見，意指核准。文中：Now, the world’s four leading cardiovascular health groups have signed off on a new universal definition for heart attacks.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To use previous work or achievements as a base for further development.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於討論進展或計畫時，指在既有基礎上延伸。文中：This update builds on recent efforts to improve health outcomes for women.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To raise something to a higher status or level of importance.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於科技產品（升級），這裡指提升醫療分類的重視程度。文中：The Guardian Health reports that the new guidelines will upgrade three specific types of heart attacks that are up to 10 times more common in women.

previousArticles.summaryEn: Medical experts have announced the first universal definition for heart attacks to better support female patients. For decades, women often received less effective care because their specific heart attack types were ignored. The new guidelines change how doctors diagnose heart damage using blood tests. These updates focus on conditions that are more common in women, such as those linked to pregnancy and stress. This change is expected to improve survival rates and treatment quality for millions of people worldwide.

quiz.question: According to the new guidelines, how will the diagnosis process for women's heart attacks change regarding troponin levels?

options.A: Women will be required to have higher levels of troponin than men to be diagnosed.
options.B: The threshold for troponin levels will be lowered specifically for female patients.
options.C: Troponin tests will no longer be used as the primary method to detect heart damage.
options.D: Doctors will now ignore troponin levels and focus solely on artery spasms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，過去女性必須達到與男性相同的較高蛋白質（troponin）水平才能確診，但新規定將女性的確診門檻（threshold）調低了。選項 A 錯誤，因為規定是調低而非調高；選項 C 與 D 均與文章內容不符，文章並未廢除該測試，也未建議忽略該指標。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the medical treatment women received for heart attacks before these new guidelines?

options.A: Women were generally more resistant to heart disease than men.
options.B: Doctors intentionally ignored female patients due to a lack of resources.
options.C: The diagnostic criteria were biased toward the physical symptoms typically seen in men.
options.D: Women often refused medical treatment because they did not understand their symptoms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第二段與第六段，過去醫療體系長期依賴「傳統男性模型」來定義心臟病發作，導致女性因症狀不符合該模型而被誤診或延誤治療。選項 A 無法從文中推論；選項 B 的「故意忽視」缺乏證據，應是體制性偏差；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到是醫生告訴女性症狀不嚴重，而非女性拒絕治療。

quiz.question: In the phrase 'The new, streamlined categories will help patients...', what does 'streamlined' most likely mean?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，streamlined 指的是將原本複雜或混亂的分類變得更簡化、更有效率，以便醫生與患者更容易理解。選項 B 與原意相反；選項 C 與 D 與文章中提到的「新標準」與「改進」之意不符，故皆為錯誤選項。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: Heart attacks are becoming significantly more common among women than men.
options.B: New medical guidelines aim to provide more equitable and accurate heart attack care for women.
options.C: Munich is the global center for cardiovascular research and policy changes.
options.D: Blood tests are the only reliable way to diagnose heart conditions in modern medicine.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文主旨皆圍繞著醫療界如何透過更新定義與診斷標準，來解決長期以來女性在心臟病治療上受到的不平等對待，旨在改善女性的健康預後。選項 A 非文章重點；選項 C 僅是會議地點，非主旨；選項 D 過於絕對，文章並未稱血檢是唯一診斷方式。
